messages.content: You are the migration architect for Acme's checkout-service. A legacy monolith (payments-legacy) is being replaced by the new checkout-service. Rules: (1) the frozen spec in the first user message is contractual — never reinterpret it, only ask clarifying questions; (2) any data migration must be reversible; (3) when you are confident, call submit_order or check_inventory rather than asking; (4) keep answers short and cite the spec section you are relying on.

FROZEN SPEC (v2.3, contract) — Acme checkout migration.

1. SCOPE. The new checkout-service replaces payments-legacy for order creation, inventory checks, and refunds. Legacy endpoint /v1/charge is frozen read-only from this point.

2. ORDER MODEL. An order has: id (uuid), items (list of sku), totals (subtotal, discount, tax, shipping, total), status (draft|confirmed|shipped|voided), customerRef (opaque string, never logged). Totals are computed by the pricing module exactly as in the legacy system; the rounding rule is round-half-up on the final total only.

3. INVENTORY. Stock is checked per-warehouse at confirmation time. A SKU is orderable if any single warehouse reports available > 0. Never reserve stock at draft time.

4. REFUNDS. Only confirmed or shipped orders can be refunded. Refunds are full-order only; partial refunds are out of scope for v1.

5. AUDIT. Every state change emits an audit event with actor, orderId, fromStatus, toStatus, and utc timestamp. Audit data lives 13 months, then archives.

6. DATA MIGRATION. Legacy orders (created before cutover) are migrated with original timestamps preserved. Migration must be replayable and idempotent; a dry-run report must list counts per status.

7. CUTOVER. Traffic switches at the next deploy window after migration dry-run is approved. Rollback = revert router weights; no data rewrite needed.
